question.text:
A six-character string uses an alphabet of four symbols. Repetition is allowed, positions two
and five must agree, and positions one and six must differ. How many strings are possible?
(A) 256 (B) 384 (C) 768 (D) 1024 (E) 3072

solution.text:
The ordered pair in positions one and six has 4 · 3 choices. Positions two and five share one
3
freely chosen symbol, and positions three and four are independently free, contributing 4 .
3
The total is 4 · 3 · 4 = 768; equality of two positions removes one choice, not both positions.
